verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The Lean never forms a 2×2 matrix object; the same linear map is carried by the two scalar coordinate right-hand sides rhsX, rhsY, whose coefficients are coeff11, coeff12, coeff21. Rewriting: set rot = 0, ρ' = 0, d = 0 (undamped), ρ = s, F = F_0, g = g_0. Then the coefficient of x in rhsX is coeff11 s 0 ⟪K,g₀⟫ - 0 = s⟪K,g₀⟫/(1+s²) = 0 (⟪K,g₀⟫ = 0, the paper's g_0 = |g_0|N), the coefficient of y in rhsX is coeff12 F₀ N_θ s 0 = 2F₀N_θ/(1+s²), the coefficient of x in rhsY is coeff21 F₀ N_θ ⟪N,g₀⟫ s 0 = -(2F₀N_θ + |g₀|), and the coefficient of y in rhsY is -d = 0 — entry for entry the paper's matrix, including the 1+s² only on the (1,2) entry ("dividing the first coordinate by 1+s²"). frame_coefficients_close and scalar_coefficients_close name exactly these three reference entries as the values the actual coefficients are compared with. The eigenvalue claim that accompanies the display is carried by reference_characteristic_equation (λ/√(1+s²) solves μ² = ab/(1+s²)) together with lambda0_div_c0 and lambda0_mul_c0, which identify a = 2F₀N_θ and b = -(2F₀N_θ + ‖g₀‖) for the constructed reference data.
